## Lists

### Example no1. Converting percentages to proportions

```{r}
percentages <- c(25, 50, 75, 90)
```

```{r}
class(percentages)
```

```{r}
print(percentages)
```

```{r}
for (pct in percentages) {
  print(pct/100)
}
```

```{r}
proportions <- c()

for (pct in percentages) {
  prop <- pct/100
  proportions <- c(proportions, prop)
}
```

```{r}
print(proportions)
```

## Sets

### Example no2. Counting categorical data

```{r}
responses <- c("UK", "Germany", "France", "Germany")
```

```{r}
countries <- unique(responses)
```

```{r}
countries
```

```{r}
for (country in countries) {
  count <- sum(responses == country)
  print(paste(country, ":", count))
}
```

## Dataframes

### Example no3. Converting raw counts into percentages

```{r}
library(readxl)
```

```{r}
df <- read_excel("data/test_data.xlsx")
```

```{r}
df
```

#### Using .iterrows()

```{r}
for (i in 1:nrow(df)) {
  percentage <- (df$n_agreed[i] / df$n_total[i]) * 100
  print(round(percentage, 2))
}
```

#### Using range() and len()

```{r}
for (i in 1:nrow(df)) {
  percentage <- (df$n_agreed[i] / df$n_total[i]) * 100
  print(paste(df$region[i], ":", round(percentage, 1), "%"))
}
```

#### Using list comprehension

```{r}
df$percentages <- round((df$n_agreed / df$n_total) * 100, 1)
```

```{r}
# OR
df$percentages <- round((df$n_agreed / df$n_total) * 100, 1)
```
